claims.text: Accelerated coupled degradation in multiphase eutectic HEAs at elevated temperature is driven by wear-induced breakup of a protective oxide or passive film at heterogeneous phase boundaries.
Film rupture exposes dissimilar phases having different electrochemical potentials.
Exposure of the dissimilar phases triggers localized galvanic corrosion.
Corrosion further degrades the microstructure and weakens the material.
Corrosion-induced weakening increases susceptibility to mechanical wear, producing a mutually reinforcing cycle.
The initial material is an as-cast, equilibrated eutectic HEA with distinct phases and well-defined phase boundaries.
Samples should be compared under combined wear-corrosion, wear-only, and corrosion-only conditions at matched elevated temperature.
The proposed test environment is approximately 800 K in a corrosive medium such as saline solution under cyclic sliding load.
An oxide or passive film forms in association with the heterogeneous multiphase interfaces.
Mechanical wear disrupts and removes the stable passive film at phase boundaries.
Multiphase chemical heterogeneity produces galvanically active interfaces and inferior corrosion resistance.
The wear-corrosion coupling produces degradation beyond the additive effects of wear and corrosion acting independently.
Combined wear-corrosion will produce a substantially higher overall degradation rate than the independent wear-only and corrosion-only baselines.
Combined exposure will increase wear volume relative to wear-only exposure.
Combined exposure will increase corrosion current density relative to corrosion-only exposure.
The coupling is expected where passive-film formation and mechanical disruption coexist under fixed corrosive-medium and loading conditions.
The exact acceleration in wear and corrosion rates is uncertain because of microstructural factors and oxide-film kinetics.
Failure of combined degradation to significantly exceed the sum of wear-only and corrosion-only degradation would falsify the proposed synergistic-degradation hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline and boundary statements call for matched environmental conditions, but the wear-only arm is assigned an inert electrolyte while the combined arm uses a corrosive environment, so the environmental settings are not identical.
